title: Restriction of an injective module resolution to an open ringed subspace
statement: Let X be a ringed space [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], U an open subspace, and F an O_X-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. If $F\to I^\bullet$ is an injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions] in O_X-modules, then $F|_U\to (I^\bullet)|_U$ is an injective resolution in O_U-modules. In particular, each $I^n|_U$ is injective.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-derived-open-restriction-adjunction-exact], restriction R preserves finite limits and finite colimits. It is additive by the existing moduleOverFunctor_additive instance. Mathlib therefore supplies R.PreservesHomology, and HomologicalComplex.quasiIso_map_of_preservesHomology makes the termwise image of the augmentation of [def-sp-injective-resolutions] a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 01E1 (lemma-cohomology-of-open), proof of part (1), exactness after restriction

proof.text: The same node gives an adjunction $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ with $j_!$ exact. The right-adjoint-preserves-injectives lemma [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives], applied to the exact functor $j_!$ and its right adjoint $j^{-1}$ between the abelian module categories, shows that each injective $I^n$ restricts to an injective $I^n|_U$.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 01E1 (lemma-cohomology-of-open), proof of part (1), extension by zero and preservation of injectives

proof.text: Use Mathlib HomologicalComplex.singleMapHomologicalComplex to identify the image under R of the complex concentrated in degree zero at F with the complex concentrated in degree zero at R(F). Precompose the mapped augmentation with the inverse of this isomorphism. Its composite is still a quasi-isomorphism, and Step 2 supplies injective terms, so these data define the required InjectiveResolution by [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Choose the equality of complexes to be reflexivity. The single-complex comparison has identity component in degree zero; hence the transported augmentation is exactly R.map (I.ι.f 0). The module-sheaf categories are already abelian by Mathlib, and no existence theorem for injective resolutions or enough-injectives hypothesis is needed.

lean.statement: theorem restrict_injectiveResolution (X : RingedSpace.{u}) (U : Opens X) (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X)) (I : InjectiveResolution F) : let R := SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X) U (∃ (J : InjectiveResolution (R.obj F)) (h : J.cocomplex = (R.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj I.cocomplex), J.ι.f 0 ≫ eqToHom (congrArg (fun K => K.X 0) h) = R.map (I.ι.f 0)) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, Injective (R.obj (I.cocomplex.X n)))
